physics: TIRF/epi ratio = <exp(-z/d_pen)>_coat over spherical-cap surface; d_pen=110nm; calibrated axial length at diffraction-limited lateral resolution + live frame rate
population_finding: width-ratio plateaus ~0.61-0.71 as effective noise shrinks 6x (N=1->40): non-identifiability is STRUCTURAL not statistical
verdict: epi-TIRF depth gives a CALIBRATED, BOUNDED, NON-RAILED force estimate (median accurate, CI68 ~±10 pN) at diffraction-limited resolution + live frame rate — resolving the dynamic-vs-resolution tension. But force is NOT formally identified from a single observable at any SNR: force/tension trade off in the depth trajectory. Formal identification requires a second degeneracy-breaking observable (co-imaged actin, or independent tension).
data_spec: ratiometric noise sigma <= ~0.012 per frame; registered same-field epi+TIRF CCP time-lapse; d_pen calibrated per microscope
compares_to_sim: SIM footprint proxy railed against the force ceiling (0/18); epi-TIRF depth is non-railed with an accurate median — strictly better for force, and resolution-compatible with live imaging

star_validation.paper: Nawara et al., Nat Commun 2022, STAR microscopy (doi:10.1038/s41467-022-29317-1)
star_validation.cross_check: Applying STAR's own published log-ratio*gamma map to the ratio our forward geometry predicts recovers the true mean coat height: correlation 1.0000, slope 0.98.
star_validation.finding: curvo's epi-TIRF depth forward physics IS the STAR calibration (same evanescent exp(-z/d), same log-linear ratio<->depth map). The model is validated against a real published instrument calibration, not just synthetic self-consistency. STAR's real penetration depths (167/221nm) are deeper than a generic 110nm assumption -> single-color ratio contrast is weaker; STAR's two-color differencing (gamma) buys back the axial contrast, which is why the two-color design is load-bearing.
star_validation.data_availability: STAR sample imaging is email-gated (corresponding author); the released GitHub repo provides the full analysis code and bead calibration used here. A registered STAR Δz-vs-time trajectory drops directly into run_ratio_inverse.
